what_to_detect: A creature affected in layer 7 by an effect that sets base power/toughness and by boosts or counters, where the setting effect applies first whatever the timestamps.
near_miss: A creature with boosts or counters and no effect setting its base power/toughness.
record_fields: gen-3 card base_pt and pt_boosts {temporary, counters}

what_to_detect: A creature whose characteristic-defining power/toughness (layer 7a) is overridden by an effect setting its base power/toughness (layer 7b).
near_miss: A creature with a characteristic-defining power/toughness and no setting effect, its power/toughness the defined value.

what_to_detect: A creature under a power/toughness switching effect, the switch applied to the values the earlier sublayers produced, whatever the timestamps.
near_miss: A creature with boosts and no switching effect.

what_to_detect: A text-changing effect (layer 3) rewrites a word in a static ability, and the rewritten static's later-layer effect applies to the objects the new word names.
near_miss: A static with no text change applying to the objects its printed word names.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions (which entities the rewritten static reaches)

what_to_detect: An effect removes all abilities from a permanent in layer 6, so the static abilities it had stop contributing to later layers (no boost, no granted keyword).
near_miss: The same static ability, not removed, contributing its boost or keyword.

what_to_detect: Within one layer an ability grant and an ability or keyword removal apply to the same object, and the one with the later timestamp wins.
near_miss: The same two effects with the timestamps the other way round, the other one winning.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions keywords (leading '-' for a removal)

what_to_detect: An ability an Aura or Equipment grants takes the later of its own timestamp and the attachment's, and wins over an earlier conflicting effect in the same layer.
near_miss: The conflicting effect with the later timestamp, which wins.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions keywords (leading '-' for a removal)

what_to_detect: An Equipment re-attached gets new timestamps for itself and the abilities granted to it, their relative order kept, so a later-granted keyword still wins over the Equipment's own keyword removal.
near_miss: A keyword removal with a later timestamp than the grant, which wins.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions keywords (leading '-' for a removal)

what_to_detect: Attaching an Equipment or Aura gives it a new timestamp, so its keyword grant or removal wins over a conflicting one attached earlier.
near_miss: The conflicting attachment made later, its effect winning.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions keywords (leading '-' for a removal)

what_to_detect: A keyword counter gets a new timestamp, with every counter of its kind on the object, when a counter of that kind is put on it, so it wins over an earlier ability removal.
near_miss: A keyword counter older than an ability removal, the object lacking the keyword.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions keywords (leading '-' for a removal)

what_to_detect: A permanent turned face up gets a new timestamp, so its static grant wins over an earlier conflicting effect.
near_miss: The permanent already face up before the conflicting effect, which then wins.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions keywords (leading '-' for a removal)

what_to_detect: A permanent that transforms gets a new timestamp, so its static grant wins over an earlier conflicting effect.
near_miss: The permanent already transformed before the conflicting effect, which then wins.
record_fields: continuous payload.contributions keywords (leading '-' for a removal)

what_to_detect: A characteristic-defining ability applies before the other effects of its layer, so a same-layer effect with an earlier timestamp still overrides it.
near_miss: The characteristic-defining ability alone in its layer, its value standing.

what_to_detect: One effect depends on another (applying it changes what the other does or applies to), so it applies after it whatever the timestamps.
near_miss: Two effects in the same layer with no dependency, applied in timestamp order.

what_to_detect: A copy effect sets a permanent's copiable values in layer 1, recorded as a name contribution, with the later layers applied on top.
near_miss: A static or effect contributing to the board with no name change.

what_to_detect: A face-down permanent has the characteristics of a nameless colourless 2/2 creature with no abilities.
near_miss: A face-up permanent, with its own characteristics.

what_to_detect: A copy effect applies to a face-down permanent in layer 1a and the face-down characteristics override it in layer 1b, so the permanent stays a nameless colourless 2/2.
near_miss: A copy effect on a face-up permanent, which takes the copied values.

what_to_detect: A copy of a face-down permanent takes the face-down copiable values and is face up with them.
near_miss: A copy of a face-up permanent, which takes its real values.

what_to_detect: A combat damage step in which a player's protection from a quality prevents damage from a source that has the quality only through a continuous effect.
near_miss: A combat damage step in which damage to a player with protection is dealt because the source lacks the quality.

what_to_detect: An attackers legality record in which a creature is required to attack because a rules-modifying static ability of an object applies.
near_miss: An attackers record in which the creature has no attack requirement because the static's source lost the ability.
